questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to study in a vibrant city which was big enough to feel like a big city but still small enough so you get to know it properly during your exchange. It was also crucial to me that it was a destination I hadn't visited before, so it would be a fresh start. It was also a very big plus that Lisbon has such nice weather, so you want to be outside for all the months of your exchange.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think the university was pretty informative. The planning of the courses was not final, so a lot of the courses that I chose ended up being on the 2nd and 3rd trimester, so I had to switch. It was no big deal though.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was two orientation days where they gave us the most important information. In general the people responsible for exchange were super open and helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I used both Facebook Marketplace and Uniplaces. I wouldn't recommend Facebook Marketplace, as there are a lot of scammers. Uniplaces is finde, but the administration fee to the platform is quite high. I would recommend finding a cheap accommodation for the first 2 weeks and then looking at apartments on Idealista. Here you can visit the apartments in person and maybe talk to the current tenant and ask how the apartment is.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The campus is not very central, so I would in general recommend living off campus, so you can live in a more exciting part of the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't check out on campus housing.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The process of registering at the university was fine. But signing up to courses was via emails, and I had to switch courses later on. There is no platform to see in which courses you are enrolled which is a bit confusing.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international office

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: The dates of the courses were not in place until the week before the semester started. Therefore I had to switch courses and the selection of courses available was therefore way smaller than what I first thought.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take it chill. Don't stress about them not giving out information in good time, cause it will often come pretty late.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took courses on the LLM

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It varied a lot. Some professors were very interactive and others were just lecturing on their own. Also, a lot of the exams were write at home-essays, which I was not used to.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Comparative Corporate Law - very interesting professor.
The law of European Integration - very good if you want to get a better understanding of how the European Union functions in real life.

Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Social activities were a bit limited, but plenty of opportunities through Erasmus or private events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Didn't participate in any

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Plenty of good trips to do: Maderia, Marrakech, Azores, Porto and Algarve Coast.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: As I'm also European it was not too difficult.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be smiling and outgoing when meeting people in classes. Especially during the first few weeks when no friend groups are really 'settled', it is pretty easy to just talk to the people sitting next to you in class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The slow approach to everything. Going to supermarkets og anything administered by the government will take time.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Openness and the food.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Make use of the good weather while you're there, do many weekend trips don't be afraid to try new things.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting so many great people of different culture. It was so amazing to explore new friendships in a new city

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Leaving

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
